question_text: According to the course material, source documents are business documents confirming the occurrence of financial transaction between two or more parties and are used for the first entries in the subsidiary books; they include invoices, receipts, debit notes, credit notes, payment vouchers, cheque books, clock cards, time sheets and:
explanation: Source documents start the books: invoices, receipts, debit/credit notes, vouchers, cheques, clock cards, time sheets, bank tellers.

question_text: According to the course material, an invoice under normal circumstance is meant for credit transactions which include credit sales and credit purchases; invoices are recorded in the sales day book or purchases day book depending if it is a sales invoice or a:
explanation: Invoice: transfer of goods/service for which payment is yet to be received.

question_text: According to the course material, a receipt is a document confirming the receipt of money for goods and service sold or bought and receipts are used in recording the cash book since it is evidence of:
explanation: Receipts record cash and cheque into the cash book.

question_text: According to the course material, a cheque is a negotiable instrument that originates from banks and is used to withdraw money from a stated bank account; it contains the name of the holder, account number, branch, bank, date, owner's signature, and amount in:
explanation: Cheque: words and figures for the amount.

question_text: According to the course material, the sales day book is used to record credit sales to a third party in the order in which they occurred; cash sales cannot be recorded there, and the total of credit sales is transferred to the credit side of:
explanation: Credit sales: debit customers, credit sales. Cash sales do not go in the sales day book.

question_text: According to the course material, cash discount is an inducement given to debtors for paying their debt on time within the specified time frame, whereas trade discount is the discount available to those who buy on credit at:
explanation: Trade discount at point of sale; cash discount for prompt payment.

question_text: According to the course material, the purchases day book records credit purchases; cash purchases cannot be recorded there; double entry is achieved by crediting the supplier's (creditor) account and debiting:
explanation: Credit purchases: debit purchases, credit creditors.

question_text: According to the course material, returns inwards relate to goods returned by customers; the returns inwards account is debited while the affected customers' accounts will be credited to:
option_a: reduce their debt to the business
explanation: Returns inwards (sales returns): reduce debtors.

question_text: According to the course material, the four journals treated for credit transactions only are sales day book, purchases day book, returns inwards and returns outwards; none of them can be used to record transfer of property since it is not a credit sale, credit purchase or:
explanation: The journal proper records other items, e.g. purchase of non-current assets on credit.

question_text: According to the course material, the journal is used for opening entries, purchase and sale of non-current assets on credit, corrections of accounting errors, adjustments and transfer of property; example: Mercy Investment bought a motor vehicle on credit for N850,000, so debit motor vehicle and credit:
explanation: Non-current asset on credit is journalised, not put through the sales/purchases day books.

question_text: According to the course material, in the cash book the left side is the debit side and the credit side is the right side; at the end of a period the postings on each side are added and the difference is:
explanation: Cash book: debit receipts, credit payments; difference is the cash balance.

question_text: According to the course material, when cash is removed from the office and paid into the bank you debit the bank column and credit the cash column; this is a contra entry represented by letter C in the folio columns, meaning a transaction recorded twice through a debit and a credit in:
explanation: Contra: debit and credit in the same account (two-column cash book). Not posted to the ledgers again.

question_text: According to the course material, the petty cash imprest system operates when the main cashier gives the petty cashier enough money to cover petty expenses for a given period; at the end of the period the petty cashier gets a reimbursement equal to the amount already spent, so the balance at the beginning of each period will always equal:
explanation: Imprest: replenish spending so opening balance equals the float.

question_text: According to the course material, a junior cashier is usually designated as petty cashier to handle payment of small expenses so as to relieve the main cashier from attending to too numerous payments; the cash provided is called petty cash and the book is the:
explanation: Petty cashier + petty cash book for small expenses.

question_text: According to the course material, double entry book-keeping means debit the receiver and credit the giver; every transaction is recorded twice so that at the end debit totals equal:
explanation: Double entry: two sides; debit receiver, credit giver.

question_text: According to the course material, a payment voucher is used to record full details of money paid for a particular purpose; it contains the name of the receiver, amount, purpose, date, mode of payment (cash or cheque), signature of the receiver, and name and signature of:
explanation: Payment voucher shows money has left an account; needs approving authority.

question_text: According to the course material, many sole traders do not know the function of an invoice to the extent that all their sales (cash and credit) are documented using invoice, whereas under normal circumstance an invoice is meant for:
explanation: Invoice is normally for credit sales and credit purchases.

question_text: According to the course material, the value of credit sales first recorded in the sales journal is transferred so that the total of all credit sales for the period is credited to sales, while individual customer amounts are:
explanation: Debit debtors, credit sales for credit sales.

question_text: According to the course material, discount allowed column is on the debit side of a three-column cash book, while discount received column is on:
explanation: Three-column cash book: discount allowed (Dr) and discount received (Cr).

question_text: According to the course material, Unit 12 of ACC203 treats double entry book-keeping systems after the subsidiary books (sales, purchases, returns, journal, cash books and petty cash); posting from books of original entry into the ledger completes:
explanation: Subsidiary books then ledger posting = double entry.

question_text: According to the course material, cash sales paid directly to bank increase the bank column; they are not recorded in the sales day book because the sales day book is for:
explanation: Sales day book: credit sales only, not cash sales.

question_text: According to the course material, clock cards and time sheets are listed among source documents used for first entries in the subsidiary books, alongside invoices, receipts, debit notes, credit notes, payment vouchers, cheque books and:
explanation: Clock cards and time sheets are source documents in the guide.

question_text: According to the course material, when cash is withdrawn from the bank for office use you debit the cash column and credit the bank column, another contra entry; this increases cash in the office while money in the bank will:
explanation: Bank to cash: debit cash, credit bank (contra).

question_text: According to the course material, trade discount given on credit sales is deducted before the net amount is recorded in the sales day book; cash discount is not recorded in the sales day book but arises when the debtor pays:
explanation: Trade discount at sale; cash discount at prompt payment.

question_text: According to the course material, purchase of a motor vehicle on credit worth N850,000 is journalised as being motor vehicle bought on credit; this cannot go through the purchases day book because the purchases day book records credit purchases of goods for:
explanation: Purchases day book is for goods on credit, not non-current assets.
